title: TNS: Decode Oracle OCI call bodies and row data
description:
This extends the Oracle TNS/TTC dissector to decode the OCI call bodies
exchanged while a query is executed, and to extract the row data returned
to the client. It builds on the TNS foundations already in master (the sb4
dispatch helper, OER/DTY, piggyback handling).

Decoded here, one self-contained commit per body:

- TTI_IOV — the I/O vector that precedes a call.
- TTI_DCB / TTI_RXH — the describe (column metadata) and the row header.
- TTI_ALL8 — the SQL-execute request: header, SQL text, and the bind
  descriptors and values (OAC).
- TTI_FETCH — the fetch-rows request body.
- TTI_LOBOPS — the LOB-operations request header.
- TNS_MARKER — labels the break/reset function.
- TTI_RXD — splits the returned row values using the column types from the
  matching describe, threaded across packets via last_describe conversation
  state; plus the ROWID / UROWID / LONG / LOB row framings.

Every body comes with a self-contained fixture generator under
test/captures/_gen_tns_*.py (no external dependencies — each emits a
byte-identical pcap) and a matching test in test/suite_dissection.py.

All decoders target the Oracle 11g wire shape, matching the existing OER
decoder. Row values are extracted as fields at this stage; human-readable
per-type rendering (NUMBER, DATE, floats, strings) follows in a later,
stacked change so this one stays reviewable.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+#
+# Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+# By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+"""Generate test/captures/tns_all8.pcap with two TTI_ALL8 (SQL execute)
+request frames:
+
+    Frame 1 — SELECT (options 0x8021 = parse+execute+fetch, fetch 15 rows):
+                "SELECT ID, NAME FROM USERS"
+    Frame 2 — DML with autocommit (options 0x8121):
+                "DELETE FROM USERS WHERE ID = 5"
+    Frame 3 — DML with two binds (options 0x8029):
+                "UPDATE USERS SET NAME=:1 WHERE ID=:2"
+                bind 1 VARCHAR "hi", bind 2 NUMBER 10 — a bare OAC per bind
+                then a TTI_RXD row of DALC values.
+
+Bytes are constructed by hand in the Oracle 11g wire shape.
+"""
+import os
+import struct
+
+# TTC tokens / OCI function ids.
+TTI_FUN = 3
+TTI_RXD = 7
+TTI_ALL8 = 94
+
+# Oracle native data-type ids.
+TYPE_VARCHAR = 1
+TYPE_NUMBER = 2
+
+
+def ub4(val: int) -> bytes:
+    """Variable-length unsigned integer in the Oracle ub4 form."""
+    if val == 0:
+        return b"\x00"
+    if val <= 0xFF:
+        return bytes([1, val])
+    if val <= 0xFFFF:
+        return bytes([2]) + struct.pack(">H", val)
+    if val <= 0xFFFFFF:
+        return bytes([3]) + struct.pack(">I", val)[1:]
+    return bytes([4]) + struct.pack(">I", val)
+
+
+def dalc(s: bytes) -> bytes:
+    return bytes([len(s)]) + s
+
+
+def oac(data_type: int, charset: int, csform: int, max_size: int) -> bytes:
+    return (
+        bytes([data_type])       # type (ub1)
+        + b"\x00"                # flag (ub1)
+        + b"\x00"                # precision (sb1)
+        + ub4(0)                 # scale (ub4)
+        + ub4(max_size)          # max data length / buffer size (ub4)
+        + ub4(0)                 # max array elements (ub4)
+        + ub4(0)                 # cont flags (ub4)
+        + ub4(0)                 # type OID (empty)
+        + ub4(0)                 # version (ub4)
+        + ub4(charset)           # charset id (ub4)
+        + bytes([csform])        # charset form (ub1)
+        + ub4(max_size)          # max size (ub4)
+    )
+
+
+def build_all8(seq: int, sql: bytes, options: int, fetch: int,
+               stmt_type: int, binds: list | None = None) -> bytes:
+    binds = binds or []
+    al8 = [options, fetch, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, stmt_type, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
+    b = bytes([TTI_FUN, TTI_ALL8, seq])
+    b += ub4(options)            # options
+    b += ub4(0)                  # cursor id (0 = new)
+    b += bytes([1])              # query present flag
+    b += ub4(len(sql))           # query length
+    b += bytes([1])              # all8 present flag
+    b += ub4(len(al8))           # all8 length
+    b += bytes([0, 0])           # two reserved bytes
+    b += ub4(0)                  # long max value
+    b += ub4(fetch)              # fetch rows
+    b += ub4(0)                  # max value
+    b += bytes([1 if binds else 0])  # bind indicator
+    b += ub4(len(binds))         # bind count
+    b += bytes([0, 0, 0, 0, 0])  # five reserved bytes
+    b += bytes([0])              # define-columns present flag
+    b += ub4(0)                  # define-columns count
+    b += bytes([0, 0, 1])        # marker
+    b += bytes([0, 0, 0, 0, 0])  # server version slot (5 bytes)
+    b += sql                     # SQL text (flat on 11g)
+    for elem in al8:             # al8i4 option array
+        b += ub4(elem)
+    if binds:
+        for data_type, charset, csform, max_size, _value in binds:
+            b += oac(data_type, charset, csform, max_size)
+        b += bytes([TTI_RXD])    # one value row
+        for _dt, _cs, _cf, _ms, value in binds:
+            b += dalc(value)
+    return b
+
+
+frames = [
+    build_all8(1, b"SELECT ID, NAME FROM USERS", 0x8021, 15, 1),
+    build_all8(2, b"DELETE FROM USERS WHERE ID = 5", 0x8121, 0, 0),
+    build_all8(3, b"UPDATE USERS SET NAME=:1 WHERE ID=:2", 0x8029, 0, 0, binds=[
+        (TYPE_VARCHAR, 873, 1, 32, b"hi"),
+        (TYPE_NUMBER, 0, 0, 22, b"\xc1\x0b"),
+    ]),
+]
+
+
+def ipv4_checksum(h: bytes) -> int:
+    s = sum(((h[i] << 8) | h[i + 1]) for i in range(0, len(h), 2))
+    while s >> 16:
+        s = (s & 0xFFFF) + (s >> 16)
+    return (~s) & 0xFFFF
+
+
+def tcp_checksum(src: bytes, dst: bytes, seg: bytes) -> int:
+    pseudo = src + dst + b"\x00\x06" + struct.pack(">H", len(seg))
+    buf = pseudo + seg
+    if len(buf) % 2:
+        buf += b"\x00"
+    s = sum(((buf[i] << 8) | buf[i + 1]) for i in range(0, len(buf), 2))
+    while s >> 16:
+        s = (s & 0xFFFF) + (s >> 16)
+    return (~s) & 0xFFFF
+
+
+def wrap(body: bytes, seq: int, ip_id: int) -> bytes:
+    # TNS DATA framing (10 bytes).
+    tns = struct.pack(">HhBBhh", len(body) + 10, 0, 6, 0, 0, 0) + body
+
+    src_ip = bytes([10, 0, 0, 1])
+    dst_ip = bytes([10, 0, 0, 2])
+    # Client -> server (requests), so dst_port is the listener port 1521.
+    tcp_no_csum = struct.pack(
+        ">HHIIBBHHH",
+        54321, 1521,
+        seq, 0,
+        0x50, 0x18, 65535, 0, 0,
+    )
+    csum = tcp_checksum(src_ip, dst_ip, tcp_no_csum + tns)
+    tcp = tcp_no_csum[:16] + struct.pack(">H", csum) + tcp_no_csum[18:]
+    seg = tcp + tns
+
+    ip_total = 20 + len(seg)
+    ip_no = struct.pack(">BBHHHBBH", 0x45, 0, ip_total, ip_id, 0x4000, 64, 6, 0) + src_ip + dst_ip
+    ip = ip_no[:10] + struct.pack(">H", ipv4_checksum(ip_no)) + ip_no[12:]
+    return ip + seg
+
+
+out = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "tns_all8.pcap")
+with open(out, "wb") as f:
+    f.write(struct.pack("<IHHIIII", 0xA1B2C3D4, 2, 4, 0, 0, 65535, 101))
+    # Cumulative TCP sequence so a smaller follow-on frame is not read as a
+    # retransmission and dropped before the TNS layer is dissected.
+    seq = 1
+    for i, body in enumerate(frames):
+        pkt = wrap(body, seq=seq, ip_id=i + 1)
+        seq += len(body) + 10
+        f.write(struct.pack("<IIII", 0, i, len(pkt), len(pkt)))
+        f.write(pkt)
+print(f"wrote {out} ({os.path.getsize(out)} bytes, {len(frames)} frames)")

+    if val <= 0xFFFFFF:
+        return bytes([3]) + struct.pack(">I", val)[1:]
+    return bytes([4]) + struct.pack(">I", val)

+    """Signed variable-length integer (sign-magnitude): the high bit of the
+    length byte flags a negative value. NUMBER scale -127 -> 0x81 0x7f."""
+    if val == 0:
+        return b"\x00"
+    b = bytearray(ub4(abs(val)))

+    return bytes(b)
+

+def dalc(s: bytes) -> bytes:
+    return bytes([len(s)]) + s
+
+
+def swl(s: bytes) -> bytes:
+    """str_with_length: a ub4 count and, when non-zero, a DALC blob."""
+    if not s:

+    return ub4(len(s)) + dalc(s)
+

+def bwl(s: bytes) -> bytes:
+    """bytes_with_length: a ub4 count and, when non-zero, a length-prefixed
+    blob. Only the empty form is needed here."""
+    if not s:
+        return ub4(0)
+    return ub4(len(s)) + dalc(s)

+        charset: int, csform: int, max_size: int) -> bytes:
+    return (
+        bytes([data_type])       # type (ub1)
+        + b"\x00"                # flag (ub1)
+        + bytes([precision])     # precision (sb1)
+        + sb4(scale)             # scale (ub4)
+        + ub4(max_length)        # max data length / buffer size (ub4)
+        + ub4(0)                 # max array elements (ub4)
+        + ub4(0)                 # cont flags (ub4)
+        + bwl(b"")               # type OID (bytes_with_length)
+        + ub4(0)                 # version (ub4)
+        + ub4(charset)           # charset id (ub4)
+        + bytes([csform])        # charset form (ub1)
+        + ub4(max_size)          # max size (ub4)
+    )
+
+

+               charset: int, csform: int, max_size: int, name: bytes) -> bytes:
+    return (
+        oac(data_type, precision, scale, max_length, charset, csform, max_size)
+        + b"\x01"                # nulls allowed (ub1)
+        + bytes([len(name)])     # v7 name length (ub1)
+        + swl(name)              # column name (str_with_length)
+        + swl(b"")               # schema name (str_with_length)
+        + swl(b"")               # type name (str_with_length)
+        + ub4(0)                 # column position (ub4)
+        + ub4(0)                 # uds flags (ub4, 11g)
+    )

+    b += ub4(80)                 # max row size (ub4)
+    b += ub4(len(columns))       # num columns (ub4)
+    b += b"\x00"                 # reserved byte (num columns > 0)

+    b += ub4(0) * 4              # dcbflag / dcbmdbz / dcbmnpr / dcbmxpr
+    b += bwl(b"")                # dcbqcky (bytes_with_length)
+    return b
+
+

+        + ub4(1)                 # num requests
+        + ub4(1)                 # iteration number
+        + ub4(num_iters)         # num iterations
+        + ub4(0)                 # buffer length
+        + ub4(0)                 # bit vector length (0 => no vector)
+        + bwl(b"")               # rxhrid (bytes_with_length)
+    )
+
+
+frames = [
+    build_dcb(),
+    build_rxh(2),
+]
+

+def ipv4_checksum(h: bytes) -> int:
+    s = sum(((h[i] << 8) | h[i + 1]) for i in range(0, len(h), 2))
+    while s >> 16:
+        s = (s & 0xFFFF) + (s >> 16)
+    return (~s) & 0xFFFF

+    buf = pseudo + seg

+    while s >> 16:
+        s = (s & 0xFFFF) + (s >> 16)
+    return (~s) & 0xFFFF

+    # TNS DATA framing (10 bytes).
+    tns = struct.pack(">HhBBhh", len(body) + 10, 0, 6, 0, 0, 0) + body

+    tcp = tcp_no_csum[:16] + struct.pack(">H", csum) + tcp_no_csum[18:]

+    f.write(struct.pack("<IHHIIII", 0xA1B2C3D4, 2, 4, 0, 0, 65535, 101))

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+#
+# Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+# By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
+# Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs
+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+"""Generate test/captures/tns_iov.pcap with two TTI_IOV frames:
+
+    Frame 1 — a PL/SQL block with 3 binds (IN, OUT, IN OUT); because two
+              binds are OUT/IN OUT a TTI_RXD row of the returned values
+              follows the direction vector.
+    Frame 2 — a block with 2 pure-IN binds; no values follow.
+
+Bytes are constructed by hand in the Oracle 11g wire shape. Only the direction vector is decoded by the dissector;
+the trailing RXD values (which need each bind's type to decode) are left
+to the generic data dissector.
+"""
+import os
+import struct
+
+# Bind directions (TNS_BIND_DIR_*).
+OUT = 16
+IN = 32
+IN_OUT = 48
+
+
+def ub4(val: int) -> bytes:
+    """Variable-length unsigned integer in the Oracle ub4 form."""
+    if val == 0:
+        return b"\x00"
+    if val <= 0xFF:
+        return bytes([1, val])
+    if val <= 0xFFFF:
+        return bytes([2]) + struct.pack(">H", val)
+    if val <= 0xFFFFFF:
+        return bytes([3]) + struct.pack(">I", val)[1:]
+    return bytes([4]) + struct.pack(">I", val)
+
+
+def dalc(s: bytes) -> bytes:
+    return bytes([len(s)]) + s
+
+
+def build_iov(directions: list[int], rxd_values: list[bytes] | None) -> bytes:
+    num_binds = len(directions)
+    num_iters, num_requests = divmod(num_binds, 256)
+    b = bytes([11])          # TTI_IOV token
+    b += b"\x00"             # flag
+    b += ub4(num_requests)
+    b += ub4(num_iters)
+    b += ub4(0)              # num iters this time
+    b += ub4(0)              # uac buffer length
+    b += ub4(0)              # fast-fetch bit vector length (0 => no bytes)
+    b += ub4(0)              # rowid length (0 => no bytes)
+    b += bytes(directions)
+    if rxd_values:
+        b += bytes([7])      # TTI_RXD token
+        for v in rxd_values:
+            b += dalc(v)     # value blob
+            b += ub4(0)      # per-value return code (0 => present)
+    return b
+
+
+frames = [
+    # IN, OUT, IN OUT -> two returned values: NUMBER 10 (c1 0b) and
+    # VARCHAR "hi!".
+    build_iov([IN, OUT, IN_OUT], [b"\xc1\x0b", b"hi!"]),
+    # Two pure-IN binds -> no RXD row follows.
+    build_iov([IN, IN], None),
+]
+
+
+def ipv4_checksum(h: bytes) -> int:

commits_data.message:
TNS: Decode ROWID / UROWID / LONG / LOB row values

Extend the TTI_RXD row decoder (which previously handled only ordinary
DALC columns and stopped at anything else) with the per-type value
framings for the columns whose wire form differs from a plain DALC,
in the Oracle 11g wire shape:

  - ROWID: a reserved-size indicator, then the physical rowid parts
    (data object, relative file, unused, block, slot), all ub4.
  - UROWID: a ub4 byte count, a length echo, then the rowid bytes.
  - LONG / LONG RAW: the value (NULL / single chunk / 0xFE-chunked) plus
    two trailing ub4 length indicators.
  - CLOB / BLOB / BFILE: a NULL marker, or a ub4 length and the DALC
    locator block.

Each value is shown as "Column N (TYPE)" with its raw bytes. Object,
JSON (OSON) and VECTOR columns carry richer image framings and still
stop the row decode, leaving the remainder to the data dissector.

Fixture pcap is synthesised: a describe of NUMBER / ROWID / LONG columns
then a row carrying one value of each, so the ROWID and LONG framings
are exercised byte-for-byte alongside the ordinary NUMBER.

Signed-off-by: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>

TNS: Decode TTI_RXD row values using the describe

A SELECT result set's row data arrives in TTI_RXD tokens whose values
are split per column according to the column types from the preceding
TTI_DCB describe — which, for a TTI_FETCH continuation, arrived in an
earlier packet. The dissector had no way to correlate the two, so RXD
row data was left opaque.

Thread the describe across packets: when a TTI_DCB is decoded, record
its per-column type list in the conversation state; a later TTI_RXD
response retrieves it (stashed per-packet for two-pass safety) and uses
it to split each row into columns. Multiple rows in one packet are
walked (each a fresh RXD token). Ordinary (DALC-framed) values are shown
raw; NULLs are labelled.

Scope: the value framings for the special types (LONG, ROWID, UROWID,
LOB / BFILE, object, JSON, VECTOR) differ from a plain DALC and warrant
their own tested follow-up, so a row stops decoding at the first such
column and leaves the remainder to the data dissector. Differential
(bit-vector) row encoding is likewise not applied.

Fixture pcap is synthesised: a two-column describe (NUMBER "ID",
VARCHAR2 "NAME") then a row-data packet of two rows — (10, "hi") and
(20, NULL) — in one server->client stream, so the RXD decode exercises
the cross-packet describe threading.

TNS: Decode TTI_LOBOPS (LOB operations) request header

LOB content transfer (read, write, get length, trim, temp-LOB
create/free, open/close, BFILE ops) multiplexes over the TTI_LOBOPS
function call, with one common request layout selecting behaviour by an
operation opcode. The dissector recognised the SQLNET_USER_OCI_FUNC
message and call id but left the body opaque.

Decode the common header in the Oracle 11g order: the pointer/length
flags, the
operation opcode (labelled against a value_string of the opcode names)
and the 1-based source offset. The opcode name is also appended to the
Info column. A CREATE_TEMP request carries a fixed field block instead
of the common header (opener 01 01 28) and is recognised as such.

The locator framing and trailing amount / write payload vary by opcode
and by persistent-vs-temporary locator variant, so they are left to the
data dissector.

(op 0x0001), both from offset 1 with a realistic 86-byte locator. Bytes
are built by hand in the same field order, so the test fails
immediately if the layout drifts.

commits_data.message:
TNS: Decode TTI_ALL8 bind descriptors and values

Complete the SQL execute request path: after the al8i4 option array a
fresh parse with binds carries one bare OAC (Oracle Access Column)
descriptor per bind column, then one TTI_RXD row of values per
iteration. The dissector decoded the execute header and SQL text but
left this bind section to the data dissector.

Decode it in the Oracle 11g order: reuse the dissect_tns_oac() helper for each bind's type descriptor
(type, precision, scale, charset, charset form, max size), then for
each TTI_RXD row show one raw value per bind as a DALC blob. Each bind
is a subtree labelled by its Oracle type; each value row is its own
subtree, so array-DML (executemany) sends several rows.

Scope: the bind values are shown as raw type-encoded bytes (full
per-type value decoding is a separate effort). Binds are only decoded on
a fresh parse (query text present) — a cached-cursor re-execute omits
the OACs and needs connection state to detect. A CLOB / BLOB bind uses a
temp-LOB locator value form that is not unpacked; those rows are left to
the data dissector.

The fixture gains a third frame: a two-bind UPDATE (VARCHAR "hi",
NUMBER 10). Bytes are built by hand in the same field order, so the
test fails immediately if the layout drifts.

TNS: Decode TTI_ALL8 (SQL execute) request body

Every SQL operation — SELECT, DML and PL/SQL — rides the TTI_ALL8
function call. The dissector recognised the outer SQLNET_USER_OCI_FUNC
message and its call id but left the execute body opaque, so the SQL
text (the single most useful field on the request path) was never
shown.

Decode the body in the Oracle 11g shape: the options word (with
a flag breakdown — parse / bind / define / execute / autocommit /
PL/SQL / fetch), the cursor id, the query and all8 present flags and
lengths, the fetch row count, the bind count, the define-columns
count, the [0,0,1] marker and 5-byte server-version slot, then the SQL
text (a flat run of query_len bytes on 11g) and the al8i4 option array.
All multi-byte integers use the ub4 variable-length helper.

The SQL text is also appended to the Info column, so a query is visible
in the packet list without expanding the tree. The bind descriptors
(OAC) and values (RXD) that can trail the al8 array need per-bind type
context to decode safely and are left to the data dissector for now.

autocommit DELETE (options 0x8121), both bind-free. Bytes are built by
hand in the same field order, so the test fails immediately if the

TNS: Decode TTI_DCB (describe) and TTI_RXH (row header) bodies

A SELECT response opens with a TTI_DCB describe (the result set's
column metadata) followed by a TTI_RXH row header. The dissector
recognised the SQLNET_DESCRIBE_INFO and SQLNET_ROW_TRANSF_HDR message
ids but left both bodies opaque.

Decode them in the Oracle 11g shape:

  - TTI_DCB (decode_token_dcb / _decode_dcb_column): skip the
    describe-info preamble, read the column count, then per column an
    OAC descriptor plus the nullability and naming fields, then skip
    the describe trailer. Each column is shown as its own subtree
    labelled "<name> (<type>)".
  - TTI_RXH (decode_token_rxh): flags, num requests, iteration number,
    num iterations, buffer length, the optional column bit vector and
    the rxhrid, exposing the counts.

The per-column metadata is the OAC (Oracle Access Column) descriptor
(§5.3), factored into a dissect_tns_oac() helper — type, precision,
scale, max data length, charset, charset form and max size — reusable
for the bind descriptors on the execute path. Data types and charsets
render via the existing value_string tables; a new value_string labels
the charset form (database vs national AL16UTF16).

get_sb4_custom gains sign-magnitude handling for the Oracle variable-
length integer: the high bit of the length byte flags a negative value
(so NUMBER's default scale -127 arrives as 0x81 0x7f). It previously
asserted-not-reached on any length byte above 4, which the describe
scale field would have hit; the width>4 counter case is handled the
way the Oracle client does.

Fixture pcap is synthesised: a 2-column describe (NUMBER "ID" with
scale -127, VARCHAR2 "NAME" in AL32UTF8) and a row header. Bytes are
built by hand in the same field order, so the test fails immediately
if the layouts drift apart.

commits_data.message:
TNS: Decode TTI_IOV (I/O vector) body

The server replies with a TTI_IOV token after executing an anonymous
PL/SQL block that carried bind variables. It lists each bind's
direction (IN / OUT / IN OUT) and, when any bind is OUT / IN OUT, is
followed by a TTI_RXD row of the returned values. The dissector
recognised the outer SQLNET_IOVEC_4FAST_UPI message id but left the
body opaque.

Decode the direction vector in the Oracle 11g order: skip the flag
byte, read num_requests and
num_iters (bind count = num_iters * 256 + num_requests) plus the
skipped counters, the fast-fetch bit vector and the rowid blob (both
length-prefixed), then one direction byte per bind. Directions are
labelled against a value_string (16 = OUT, 32 = IN, 48 = IN OUT).

The leading counters use the existing get_sb4_custom ub4 helper. The
trailing RXD returned values need each bind's declared type to decode,
which only the cursor knows, so they are left to the generic data
dissector.

Fixture pcap is synthesised: two frames, one PL/SQL block with
IN/OUT/IN OUT binds (with a trailing RXD row) and one with two pure-IN
binds. Bytes are constructed by hand in the same field order, so the
test fails immediately if the layouts drift apart. The
generator uses cumulative TCP sequence numbers so a smaller follow-on
frame is not mistaken for a retransmission and dropped before the TNS
layer is dissected.
